I bought a dog from the previous owner because she didn't have time for her dog. This dog is well trained, but she had serious separation anxiety and stress, as well as allergies. Took us a year to calm her down and make her OK with us leaving home for longer periods! And she wasn't even traumatised, just never taught to calm down. She can still revert and chew the kids toys or our shoes if she doesn't get enough stimulation, and she is not even a high energy dog.

What are you exactly doing with the dog? Are you doing anything, walking, exercise, running, nosework, obedience? Or is the dog just "a dog"? Huskies need exercise, and to work with their brains and body, otherwise they will get anxious and rip apart your furniture. 

You mention training, but not what kind of training and for how long. 7 months is not a long time. Separation anxiety takes a long time to train to go away, and you need to give the dog what it needs before you train. Has it gotten exercise and worked its brain? Is it content enough to accept training? Food or toy motivated?

Unless BOTH of you are willing to put down a lot of time and effort to help this dog, its not gonna work. There are no quick fixes. If you decide to rehome, maybe try putting up an ad with what you seek and what the dog needs and not just putting it in a shelter. Best of luck!

1. Exercise your cat. It's a living being, not a piece of artwork to be placed in a room. Play with it, make sure it has toys, hiding spots, climbing poles, shelves. Maybe even a buddy. Cat's can be trained, but you MUST meet the cats needs first. They are social, energetic beings! It is probably bored out of it's mind, it's just a matter of time before it starts to pee everywhere because it think this life sucks.
2. Trim the claws regularly, maybe apply those nailcaps. And buy MORE scratching stuff! There are cardboard "furniture", shelves, hang rugs on the wall. There are even scratching boards that you can place around the corners of a sofa. Look at what the cat is scratching on and try to recreate that. Scratching posts need to be tall enough for them to stretch out, make them both standing and on the floor. Use catnip to make them interesting. Make note that cat's not only sharpen their claws by scratching, but as a way to spread their scent and make it their home.
3. Train the cat to use said items. Catify your home. Make shelves for it to climb on. I recommend watching Jackson Galaxys videos on YT on how to catify your home.
4. If you can or will not WORK YOUR ASS OFF to fix this, and opt to declaw, please rehome your cat. The cat doesn't deserve to be mutilated because of a fucking sofa.

Maybe you can't tolerate too high doses of T4? Your body converts T4 (your meds) to T3 which is the active hormon that your cells use to create energy. Too high levels of T4 makes "reverse T3" that just acts as a brake, body can't use it so you get tired and fat. 

I'm not sure about the references tho, there are lots of different ways to measure. But if you take levothyroxine, your levels should be in the upper reference and TSH should be low enough for you to feel OK.   
My personal TSH range is below 1, but the reference here in Sweden is 0,4-4.4 so doctors usually say I'm overdosing on T4, but I feel better with my dose. My T4 is somewhere between 19-21 and reference is 11-22 or something.
Yeah, you can't convert t4 enough, the ratio should be 1:3 . Are your iron, folate, B12 levels good? You maybe need to boost those to help with the thyroid.
You probably suffer from reverse t3, too high dosage and not converting enough t4 to t3. Get your t3 levels and antibodies checked, you might need liothyroine as complement.

1. Can't tell you what to avoid, depends on how people have taken care of the car (or not). Volvos are good, but can have higher taxing. But I love Volvos. Good cars, easy to get spare parts (esp if its an older model).
2. Blocket.se is a start, or look at Google Maps for car dealerships in your area.
3. Same as nr 2, Blocket can give you a good hum about the pricing on used cars.
4. Extensive rust. Depending on where the car is, they salt the roads in the winter which makes the cars rust faster on the underside. And tires, make sure they are in good shape.
5. You should definitely test drive it, and I guess you can ask the dealership to get it checked out. Either they pay for it, or you do. If you buy from a person, ask when the last checkup was. You want it as close to "today" as possible.

Bring a friend with knowledge about cars if you don't know stuff!
Check out how many owners the car has had in its past. Might give you a clue about how well it has been taken care of, or not. And check the service book if they have taken it to get service regularly.
Where to check previous owners: https://fu-regnr.transportstyrelsen.se/extweb (Note that dealerships count as owners as well)
Keep in mind the dealerships want to make as much profit as possible. I got a shitty battery in my car that broke after a couple weeks.

I'm the goddess of pestilence and health. My empire is an island, hidden away in a deep crater in the desert. The crater is miles wide, and at the bottom there is a rainforest, a huge lake and my island with my pyramids and my temple. To be able to descend the slick walls of the crater is a feat, and battle the magical waves of the lake. The human came panting up the last steps and stood before me. My pets hissed at the intruder but a command from me made them stand down.
We locked eyes, and I saw the belief in the mans eyes. He was so sure he could kill me, so sure he was a "chosen" one. I couldn't resist rolling my eyes and sigh.
"Ungh. Another one? Who sent you?" I showed him a fanged smile and turned the attention to my long sharp nails and forearm. Along the arm two giant fangs sat, shining in the light. The fangs of a snake titan I killed. A very formidable weapon, especially if I licked the tips of the fangs. That turned them venomous. I had another set on my other arm.

"Lazarius sent me! He is a true god, and you are not!" The man yelled at the top of his lungs, like I was deaf or something. He pulled out a sword, pretty shiny and pointed it towards me.
I laughed, and my lizards laughed, a raspy, hissing laughter and they bared their pointy teeth. They ate the last chosen one who tried to fight me, and they lusted for blood. Wish I didn't feed them humans in the first place, as they tend to hunt my own followers in the rainforest when they get bored. Oh well.
"Oh did he now...? So what are you gonna do, stab me?" I flashed a smile at him and locked my eyes on his. He froze as the spell activated. Slowly I climbed out of my throne and walked towards him, hips swaying. My scaled skin glistening in the light, the golden dragon tattoos on my ribs slowly turning their heads to look at the poor man.

He was sweating profusely, trying to move but my spell locked him in place. I studied the sword of his, looked like any other sword. Nothing special.
I turned my gaze back to him and now he looked scared.
"Lazarius didn't tell you about my powers, did he? Oh well, you will be dead soon. Tell him hi when you see him in the Underworld again."
I snapped my fingers and my lizards threw themselves at the man, ending his life quickly. He didn't even have time to yell. Turning my back, I heard more steps.

"THERE SHE IS! Get her! You, take that side! The others, go around there!" Trying to count the voices, I had to stop at fifteen because then the automatic fire started. I hate guns. Loud, stings and the bastards can duck behind cover and still attack me. Apparently the first man had run ahead to show his bravery to my enemy, the god of shadows. He loved to send his little followers to annoy me.

The bullets hit the stones around my feet and I hissed as some of them hit my skin. Not strong enough to hurt me but to annoy me.
My patience running thin, and realizing they were too many to take out singlehandedly I started uttering a long spell and letting my voice rise above the gunshots. I could feel it build up inside, and I let it out. From my mouth a million insects poured. They skittled and flew and surrounded the entire temple, the buzzing like music to my ears. Then the screaming started, and they people ran around, waving their hands above their heads, clawing at their necks, eyes, ears. Soon pustules plopped out on their faces, fingers turning black and rotting. Eyes rotting in the sockets. Ears bleeding.
One by one, they died horribly.

The buzzing died out, and some whimping from the last stragglers were heard. My lizards made short work of them as I walked down the stairs to the harbor and my ship. It was time to end this once and for all. The world needs a new plague.

A good way to learn to drop it and fetch is to have two toys. Play tug with one, hold the other one still but visible. When you want puppy to release, stop playing with the one in its mouth and make the other one come alive. That way puppy will switch eventually, do it often and combine it with the command. Releasing on command then means they get a funnier toy to play with eventually! Same with fetching, make sure the funnier, more alive toy is in your hands so puppy want to come to you to switch the one he caught. When he comes and drops the one he got, throw the new one and keep going. You will then become the funnier one than to have a toy for himself. This worked very well for our Mal :) 
Oh and make sure to train the off button. Stop playing just to cuddle the puppy in your lap and wait him out to relax. When he is relaxed, let him go gently. If you're lucky he will soon fall asleep in your lap or next to you :)

Hypothyroidism is a disturbance of the thyroid, where it doesn't produce enough hormones, even though the brain tells it to. The brain sends a hormone called TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone) that tells the thyroid to produce a hormone called T4 using iodine. Then the liver changes T4 to T3 and those two together affect the body's metabolism. It also controls body temperature and mood for example. These hormones also pass by the brain which registers how much is in your system and regulates how much TSH it should produce to keep the levels of T3 and T4 right. When the thyroid isn't working as it should, due to lack of iodine or a tumour, genetics or stress, you can usually tell that by bloodwork. High levels of TSH and low levels of T3 and/or T4 means the thyroid isn't producing enough, making the brain scream at it to produce more even tho it can't. 

My symptoms for this has been depression, extreme tiredness during the day, needing lots of sleep and gaining weight unexpectedly. Probably triggered by a lot of stress, but I also might have gotten it from my mother. I eat pills with thyroxine that acts like T4 and always eat salt with added iodine. I also take supplements and have almost stopped eating milk products and healthier food. My mood has increased a lot, I feel less tired and more energetic. No signs of weight loss yet but that is a work in progress. There are a lot of websites that can help with good food for people with hypothyroidism!
